column6: older text: Q4 answer lists horses among Fertile Crescent domesticates (horses were domesticated on the steppe)
inequality bullet: "stratification not found at forager sites" overstated (ranked foragers exist); copied from Explainer
workers bullet dropped where (South Korea, Taiwan) and implied wages did not rise; real wages rose fast
older text: Core Idea states the impossible trinity as gold standard/fixed rates/independent policy; it is fixed rates/capital mobility/independent policy
only the dollar was tied to gold imprecise (par values were expressed in gold); now "only the dollar was convertible, for official holders"
demand bullet overstated ("built on purpose", wages folded in); obsolescence correction implied durability-limited products are a myth
most worked as sharecroppers and were held in debt overstated; now many, sharecroppers or tenants, often in debt
older text: Explainer says world population was "stable at 1-2 billion for centuries"; it was under 1 billion before about 1800
Mosaic listed as a commercial breakthrough; it came from publicly funded NCSA; replaced with Netscape
justice bullet dropped where (evidence is from US studies); style: banned word "landscapes" replaced
Sen showed for the contested Bengal 1943 supply claim (now "argued", debate noted); "policy decides" absolute
older text: Q3 explanation says "offshore domestically", a contradiction
adjustment bullet gave price/wage deflation as the only channel (capital flows and bank rate also adjusted); added "often"
Hoover's spending cuts wrong: federal spending rose 1929-32; replaced with the 1932 tax increase. older text: Core Idea and Explainer repeat Hoover austerity
same Hoover austerity claim; "showed" softened to "suggest" (1937 also had monetary tightening)
core business was bulk necessities left out cloth, a leading Hansa good by value; furs and wax added
older text: Explainer credits the Medici with inventing the letter of credit; they did not
Glass-Steagall was only partly repealed (1999)

said the pool failures explain why Bismarck made insurance compulsory; the file says his motive was political. older text: Q3 is true-false with a what-question; Explainer calls the 1906 SF earthquake a shipping loss
social insurance "covers everyone" false for Bismarck-era schemes; copied from Explainer
older text: Q3 is true-false with a what-question
Song state issuance began in the 1020s; 10th-century notes were private Sichuan notes
older text: Q3 is true-false with a what-question; Core Idea calls a same-rate tax "regressive" by definition
older text: Q3 is true-false with a what-question
helped wreck India's textile industry overstated; hand spinning and the export trade collapsed, mills grew later
decline was mostly 1914-1950, not to 1980; Britain did not abolish hereditary privilege (hereditary peers); both copied from Explainer
older text: Q3 is true-false with a why-question
South Africa has an unusually small informal sector for its income; replaced with Mexico (copied from Q1 explanation)
US unions were not "less political"; they lacked a labor or socialist party
older text: Q0 option says output rose about 50%, explanation says 33%
risk-spreading explanation of scattered strips is a contested thesis, stated as fact
silver as the sole cause of the price rise overstated; now "helped raise"
